headline: US Agencies Unite in Rare Agreement That Blacklist Was Someone Else's Job
subheadline: *Treasury, Commerce and the White House issue joint statement declining to issue a joint statement.*
author: Marcus Bellamy-Price, Beltway Desk
seoTitle: Washington Can't Agree Who to Blame for Nvidia
seoDescription: Satire: after the Nvidia fallout, the Treasury, Commerce Department and White House each insist blacklisting Megaspeed was somebody else's lunch to lose.
sourceEvent: US government agencies are publicly squabbling over the fallout after Nvidia chief Jensen Huang stepped down in disgrace. The Treasury says it wanted to blacklist Singapore firm Megaspeed — run by suspected Chinese spy Alice Huang, who reportedly had an affair with Jensen Huang — but the Commerce Department did not act.

social.x: BREAKING: In a historic show of unity, Treasury, Commerce and the White House have all agreed on one thing — the Nvidia blacklist was absolutely somebody else's job. Full report:
social.facebook: Washington has finally found bipartisanship. The Treasury, the Commerce Department and the White House spent the week in perfect alignment, each calmly explaining that blacklisting the Singapore firm at the centre of the Nvidia scandal was a different building's responsibility. Sources confirm the memo itself was last seen riding the Metro.
social.linkedin: This week's inter-agency response to the Nvidia fallout offers a masterclass in distributed accountability: a decision architecture in which every stakeholder held veto power over everyone else's ownership. Our full analysis of the blame-routing workflow below.
social.instagram: Treasury: we sent it. Commerce: we never got it. White House: we are monitoring the situation. The memo: currently living its best life in a filing cabinet nobody checks. #satire #nvidia #washington #bureaucracy #politics
altHeadlines: Blacklisting Memo Last Seen Boarding the Metro, Refusing to Comment
Government Forms Interagency Task Force to Determine Originating Desk

body:
WASHINGTON — In a rare display of cross-government coordination, the Treasury Department, the Commerce Department and the White House moved in near-unison this week to confirm that the failure to blacklist Megaspeed, the Singapore firm at the centre of the Nvidia scandal, was definitively another agency's responsibility.

The fallout follows the resignation in disgrace of Nvidia chief Jensen Huang, whose departure has left Washington confronting its most feared adversary: a decision with no forwarding address.

Treasury officials explained that they had prepared a full blacklisting recommendation for Megaspeed — the company run by Alice Huang, a suspected Chinese spy who reportedly had an affair with the Nvidia boss — and transmitted it to Commerce using the government's standard inter-agency courier, a system formally known as 'email'.

'We sent it,' said a Treasury spokesperson. 'It is no longer in our outbox, and under federal guidelines, anything not in your outbox is legally someone else's problem.'

Commerce pushed back, noting the request had arrived in a format the department does not recognise, and possibly as a calendar invitation. 'We did receive *a* document,' conceded a senior Commerce official, speaking on condition of anonymity because the cafeteria was out of sandwiches. 'It was marked urgent, which is how we knew it was meant for Treasury.'

The White House, for its part, announced it was 'monitoring the situation closely', a status administration veterans confirmed ranks just below 'forming a working group' and just above 'reading about it in the newspaper'. An aide clarified that monitoring does not, under any reading of the relevant memorandum, include acting.

To resolve the impasse, the National Security Council has convened an Interagency Task Force on Determining the Originating Desk, which held its first session on Thursday and successfully agreed on the location of its second session. The task force's founding charter, seen by reporters, lists 'deciding who decides' as both its mission and its sole output.

'Everyone is pointing at everyone else, which is actually a sign the system is working,' said one Washington analyst. 'The founding fathers designed checks and balances specifically so that no single American could ever be reached for comment.'

Meanwhile, sources described the original blacklist memo as 'still in transit', last logged crossing a lobby somewhere between two buildings that share a coffee vendor and a mutual distrust.

A congressional aide said lawmakers planned hearings to establish a timeline, a responsibility matrix and, if time allows, a scapegoat.

At press time, the three agencies had jointly drafted a strongly worded letter of concern addressed to 'Whom It May Concern', which the Postal Service promptly returned to sender.
